objective: Building a portfolio management plan covering roles, escalation procedures, risk tolerances, thresholds, and prioritization model
secondaryObjectives: Defining or modifying portfolio processes: benefits realization, information management, risk, stakeholder engagement, and change management
Making and obtaining approval for portfolio decisions (components, plans, budget, roadmap) through the defined governance model

sources.cite: PMI, Portfolio Management Professional (PfMP) Examination Content Outline (PRA-206-2017, July 2017): Strategic Alignment 25%, Governance 20%, Portfolio Performance 25%, Portfolio Risk Management 15%, Communications Management 15%
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 through a summarizing fetch of a copy of PMI's PDF hosted by a training provider. Relevant text: Strategic Alignment Task 5 scenarios 'in order to evaluate and select viable options'; Task 6 'Recommend portfolio scenario(s) and related components, based on prioritization analysis/criteria'; Task 7 'Determine the impact to portfolio and portfolio components due to changes in strategic goals and objectives'; Portfolio Performance Task 6 'Balance portfolio and prioritize portfolio components, using established criteria and methods'; Task 7 'Analyze and optimize the consolidated allocation/reallocation of capacity'; Governance Task 5 'Make recommendations and obtain approval regarding portfolio decisions'. Whether PMI has a newer outline was not checked. The objective wording is the course seed's. Reused for REQ-336 from this course's pfmp-water-utility-rebalance (the same reading and date); the objective wording is the course seed's.

The organization, the portfolio or program, the figures and the people are fictional. The minutes or days each step takes and the effects of each decision are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values.

brief.situation: You set up portfolio management for Marlow University, a fictional university, covering 40 IT and estates initiatives. Decisions today are made by whoever shouts loudest at the vice-chancellor's meeting.
handover: No prioritization model; faculties lobby directly.
No benefits tracking after projects close.
howItWorks: The board shows the risk register against the appetite, each stakeholder's support in words and the docket.
Move on a fortnight at a time. A decision comes to you at each board meeting; before the first, you can read the evidence.
At the end you write the record and a short reflection.

parts.modelAnswer: The plan sets who decides at what threshold, how to escalate, the risk tolerances and a model that scores proposals against our four strategic goals.

parts.criteria: Benefits, change, risk and information processes; the first decision through the model.
parts.modelAnswer: Benefits are measured and reviewed after closure; changes go through the portfolio process. The lab refit was scored and deferred by the board.

scoring.modelReasoning: Portfolio governance is defined in a portfolio management plan: roles, decision thresholds, escalation procedures, risk tolerances and a prioritization model tied to strategy. Portfolio processes (benefits realization, change, risk, information) make it work, and decisions are made and recorded through the model; exceptions and self-approvals above thresholds undo it.
